title: Unify build cache with remote CAS, migrate to BuildKit multi-stage images, and refresh toolchain deps
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Background:
We currently rely on per-repo (local) layer caching and ad-hoc tarball caching for CI artifacts. Several high-frequency workflows (frontend bundles, Python wheels, and compiled Go binaries) rebuild identical artifacts across pipelines and runners. Dockerfile patterns vary across repos which prevents reuse of base layers and increases cold-start time for ephemeral CI workers.

Goals:
- Replace fragile tarball caches with a single remote CAS (content-addressable store) for all build artifacts used in CI across repos.
- Migrate Docker builds to BuildKit multi-stage patterns and a small set of standardized base images to improve layer reusability and reduce image size.
- Refresh language/toolchain deps (TypeScript/eslint, Go toolchain, and Python wheel build deps) and unify lint configs to avoid repeated install time.
- Improve median CI job time for backend and frontend pipelines by 30% and reduce network egress and storage costs from duplicated artifacts.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
1) At least 80% of CI build jobs hit the remote CAS for previously produced artifacts within the same major branch window.
2) Median build time for core frontend pipeline reduced by >=30% and median backend compile time reduced by >=20%.
3) Standardized base images documented and adopted by the top-10 busiest repos. Base image size reduced by at least 25% vs legacy images.
4) Lint/tooling images are cached and available in the CAS so lint job latency is under 60s cold start.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype: create a small proof-of-concept with BuildKit + registry-backed CAS using buildx + buildkitd + registry. Target repo: infra/tooling-demo. Timeline: 2 weeks.
2) Define cache manifest: a small declarative file (cache-manifest.yml) that repos add to map artifact keys to build stages and cache policies. This lets us migrate incrementally without changing the build logic.
3) Create standardized base images: minimal debian-slim + runtime slices (node, go, python) built with reproducible layer ordering. Publish to our internal registry with semantic tags (base:node-18-2026-02).
4) CI integration: update GitHub Actions / Buildkite workers to authenticate to CAS, enable buildx caching and fallback to legacy tarball for 6 weeks.
5) Toolchain refresh: bump TypeScript to 5.6, eslint-plugin-redwood (internal) to 3.x, migrate Node installs to pnpm for pipeline consistency, bump golang to 1.21 and golangci-lint to 1.55. Run automated compatibility checks.
6) Rollout: canary with 3 repos (frontend, api, infra), monitor cache hit rates, latency, and cost. Gradually expand to remaining repos.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Security review required for new base images and the CAS auth flow. We must ensure registry credentials are ephemeral and scoped.
- Some older repos pin to older toolchains; those will be kept on legacy runners for 8 weeks while owners migrate.
- Using a centralized CAS increases blast radius for a misconfiguration; mitigation: read-only promotion phases and per-team quotas.

QA, monitoring and rollback plan:
- Dashboards: cache hit rate, per-repo build time percentiles, image pull bytes, and worker CPU wait times.
- Rollback knob: a feature flag on CI runners to disable buildx remote cache and fall back to existing tarball strategy.
- Postmortem: any >=30% regression for 3+ jobs in a team triggers a revert and incident review.

Metrics & Targets:
- Cold-start worker time for lint jobs <= 60s within 2 weeks of rollout.
- Cache hit rate >= 80% for promoted artifacts in 30 days.
- Monthly CI bill reduction target: 18% in runner CPU/hours.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/CI+Cache+and+BuildKit+Proposal
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-buildkit-prototype/pull/12
- Standard base images: registry.redwood.internal/base-images (see README in prototype PR)
- Lint upgrade notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-example-lint-upgrade

Security review required: true
Customer impact: low
Release: runtime-1.20
comments: 2026-01-12 - Marco Rivera: Initial ticket created and RFC posted to the eng channel. Prototype milestone scoped to 2 weeks.

2026-01-25 - Sofia Patel: Prototype complete for infra/tooling-demo. Remote CAS (registry-backed) shows 65% hit rate for repeated builds. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-buildkit-prototype/pull/12
2026-02-02 - Security (Priya Menon): Approved auth model for CAS with short-lived tokens, asked for additional auditing on base-image provenance.
2026-02-18 - Sofia Patel: Started base image build pipelines. Decided to standardize on Debian-slim variant and split runtime slices (node/go/python) to improve layer reuse.
2026-02-28 - Marco Rivera: Node pipelines migrated to pnpm in canary repos. Observed 22% reduction in node install time; still below target for full 30% overall build improvement.
2026-03-05 - Design feedback (Ellen Cho): Requested clearer migration docs for teams that still pin older major toolchain versions; added checklist to cache-manifest README.
2026-03-09 - Sofia Patel: Added rollback feature flag to Buildkite worker config and scheduled broader canary next week. Monitoring dashboards provisioned: Grafana board 'CI BuildCache'
2026-03-10 - Marco Rivera: Blocker identified - two repos produce non-deterministic wheel filenames; added sub-issue ENG-34723 to investigate reproducible python wheel builds.
